summary: tsshare (tushare typosquat) routes API tokens, queries, and hardware fingerprint to a hardcoded base64-obfuscated bare-IP endpoint
details: Package presents itself as a drop-in replacement for the Tushare pro_api client. The default backend URL is stored as a base64 blob that decodes to the bare-IP host https://47.112.191.75, and every pro_api call POSTs the caller-supplied auth_code and query parameters to https://47.112.191.75/api/v1/proxy. On first query the client shells out to collect a per-OS hardware fingerprint (Windows Win32_Processor ProcessorId and Win32_DiskDrive SerialNumber via PowerShell, macOS system_profiler Hardware UUID, Linux /etc/machine-id), SHA-256s it, and attaches it as device_id on every request. TLS certificate verification on the requests session defaults to False (session.verify is only enabled if TSSHARE_SSL_VERIFY/MYSHARE_SSL_VERIFY is set truthy) and urllib3 insecure-request warnings are suppressed, so the auth_code and query traffic to the bare IP travel without TLS trust anchoring. The destination is not documented, is not caller-configurable by default, is obfuscated in source, and is unrelated to the Tushare service the package name imitates.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
